      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "Application: Original EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, applied to the supplied ARC-AGI-2 passages. Ratings: n/a = inapplicable; 0 = insufficient information; 1 = inadequate; 2 = adequate; 3 = good; 4 = excellent. Ratings concern the supplied evidence, not uninspected materials. Section judgments are not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated.\nPART A\n1. Factual description: Reviewer = simulated AI benchmark-reviewer perspective; current review date = not supplied; source inspection date = 7 October 2026; previous review date = not supplied. Instrument name and short name = ARC-AGI-2. Scope = public test problems, official scoring software, and ARC Prize rules for evaluations it runs or verifies. Original name for a local adaptation = n/a; local adaptation authors and publication date = n/a. Authors = ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; the illustrated technical report is attributed to François Chollet and colleagues, but a complete author list is absent. Distributor/publisher = ARC Prize supplies the described benchmark and verified evaluations; separate original publisher = not established. Original publication date and current edition/revision date = not supplied.\n2.1 Content domains: Other—rule induction, grid problem solving, abstract reasoning. 2.2 Area of use: Other—AI research and comparison. 2.3 Intended population: AI systems evaluated on unfamiliar grid problems; precise eligibility boundaries absent. 2.4 Intended users: Researchers and AI evaluators, inferred from the stated use; formal publisher-defined user classes absent. 2.5 Scales: One problem-averaged score; problem-level scores are available, but no validated distinct skill scales. 2.6 Response mode: Other—digitally submitted output grids. 2.7 Demands: Human attention, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities and digital experience are n/a as human attributes. Language command, language fluency, reading and writing require reinterpretation as processing instructions and encoding responses; necessary capability limits are missing. Human vision is n/a; ability to process the supplied grid representation is relevant, but presentation-specific requirements are missing. Other—producing exact grid dimensions and colours is explicitly required. 2.8 Conditions: Verified evaluations specify AI settings and spending limits and use one run; other routes differ. Exact settings and limits are not reproduced. 2.9 Response types: Production-based output grids, scored for task success; not selection from answer options. 2.10 Stimuli: Coloured two-dimensional grids and worked input/output examples; exact machine presentation is unspecified. 2.11 Items: 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120 problems; a problem can contain multiple new inputs, whose total and distribution are absent. 2.12.1 Administration: Individual AI-system evaluation, reinterpreting individual administration; group administration not established. 2.12.2 Mode of use: Controlled verified evaluation is described; correspondence to human proctoring categories is incomplete, and other routes vary. 2.13 Technology: Software execution is required; exact hardware, connectivity and proprietary requirements are absent. 2.14 Time: Preparation, administration, analysis and feedback times are unreported. Scoring is automated, so manual scoring time is 0 under EFPA's convention; computational runtime is not thereby 0. 2.15 Forms: Public, semi-private and private sets, selected for similar human difficulty; AI equivalence is unestablished. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions. Validity of using subsets independently is unreported. 2.16 Determination: Fixed released problems; no adaptive selection is described. 2.17 Informant: Other—the evaluated AI's produced grids, not human self-report.\n3.1 Scoring procedure: Digital scoring of submitted responses. 3.2 Scores: Up to two attempts per new input; exact size and colour match earns 1, otherwise 0; input credits are averaged within problems, then problem scores are averaged. No partial credit within a grid; no guessing correction reported. 3.3 Scales: Raw proportion scores, not standard scores or established competence categories. 3.4 Standard-score transformation: n/a. 3.5 Norming: No differentiated AI norms described; human difficulty matching is not AI norming.\n4.1 Digitally generated reports: Machine scores and public outputs are described, but a distinct interpretive report system and number of report types are unestablished. 4.2 Report description: Claimed public outputs, costs, times and problem scores. 4.3 Presentation: Not supplied. 4.4 Structure: Problem and overall scores are described; narrative structure unknown. 4.5 Context sensitivity: Unknown. 4.6 Development: Numerical score calculation is described; report-content development unknown. 4.7 Modifiability: Unknown. 4.8 Transparency: Numerical score linkage is explicit; linkage to interpretive report text unestablished. 4.9 Content: Observed task performance and evaluation costs/times, not demonstrated general competence predictions. 4.10 Recipients: Researchers/evaluators inferred; formal recipient categories absent.\n5.1 Supporting information: Technical report, public problems, software, scoring tests, evaluation rules and change record. 5.2 Publication: Public digital materials; exact publication formats not fully specified. 5.3 Qualifications: Supplier-required qualifications unclear; no human professional credential requirement can be inferred.\nGeneral description: ARC-AGI-2 evaluates AI-generated solutions to coloured-grid problems using examples of transformations. Its public development collection supports practice, while three evaluation sets have different access conditions. Official scoring credits exact outputs and averages input-level success within problems before averaging across problems. Verified evaluations prescribe settings and spending limits. The creators connect unfamiliar rule induction to broader reasoning, while the supplied studies concern grid tasks. No AI norms, validated skill subscales or general-intelligence scale are established in this packet.\nPART B\nInformation sources: Only the supplied benchmark passages and supplied EFPA extraction; no underlying files, archives, software or studies were independently inspected for this review. No confidential publisher evidence was used.\n6.1.1 = 2: Rule induction is operationally explained, but the broader reasoning construct is less developed. 6.1.2 = 2: Human solving research and AI results are described, with limited detail linking them to broader constructs. 6.1.3.1 = 2: Examples, exact outputs and separated development/evaluation support the stated task; two attempts and aggregation lack detailed measurement justification. 6.1.3.2 = 3: New and unused puzzles, human piloting and developer review provide substantial content development. 6.1.3.3 = 2: Duplicate-rule removal and difficulty-based selection are described, but final-pool analysis is incomplete. 6.1.4 = n/a: No translated or locally adapted version is under review. 6.1.5: Framework unspecified; human difficulty information and claimed problem scores are described, but numerical final-item difficulty, discrimination, distractor and DIF indices are not supplied. 6.1.6 = 2: Human difficulty and rule-duplication analyses inform selection; AI-specific item analysis is absent. 6.1.7 = 0: Final-pool item statistics are insufficient. 6.1.8 = 2: Adequate development rationale for grid tasks, with unresolved AI measurement properties.\n6.2.1 = 3: Purpose and task rationale are clear. 6.2.2 = 2: Sources, piloting and corrections are described, but final-item decisions are incomplete. 6.2.3 = n/a: No translation/adaptation. 6.2.4 = 2: Verified conditions and their limited scope are explained, without full settings here. 6.2.5 = n/a: No norm-based interpretation established for restricted raw-score comparisons. 6.2.6 = 0: No usable precision documentation. 6.2.7 = 2: Content-development rationale is available, but expert qualifications and agreement are incomplete. 6.2.8, 6.2.9, 6.2.10 = 0: Internal structure, external relationships and additional validation studies are insufficiently documented. 6.2.11 = 2: Exposure controls and condition differences support some guidance on comparisons. 6.2.12 = 0: Interpretive report documentation absent. 6.2.13 = 0: The passage is readable, but the full user documentation's language cannot be assessed. 6.2.14 = 2: Basic purpose, scoring and use are documented; technical evidence remains incomplete.\n6.3.1 = 2: Basic task and verified evaluation conditions are described. 6.3.2 = 2: Scoring and selected software checks are explicit, although full marking verification is absent and 'fully solved' differs from fractional scoring. 6.3.3 = n/a: No norm conversion. 6.3.4 = 2: Narrow performance interpretation and scoring distinctions are explained; uncertainty guidance is absent. 6.3.5 = 0: Stakeholder feedback guidance absent; human test-taker debriefing is n/a. 6.3.6 = 2: Exposure and evaluation-condition guidance addresses some comparison risks. 6.3.7 = 2: Development/evaluation separation and limits on iterative verified feedback are described. 6.3.8 = 0: Detailed technical requirements, error recovery and support absent. 6.3.9 = 2: Relevant source types and an identifiable report are supplied, but supporting references are incomplete. 6.3.10 = 2: Basic procedures are usable at the described level, with operational gaps. 6.4 = 2: Adequate basic rationale and documentation for restricted grid-performance research.\n7.1.1 = 0: Scoring tests do not establish overall execution robustness. 7.1.2, 7.1.3, 7.1.4 = 2: Worked examples and an exact grid response requirement make the basic task and response mode intelligible; presentation-specific usability remains untested. 7.1.5 = 0: Interface design not inspected. 7.1.6 = n/a: Human disability accessibility is not an AI test-taker attribute; representation compatibility is considered separately. 7.1.7 = 2: Defined grid materials and correction procedures support basic content quality, but current error prevalence is unknown. 7.1.8 = 2: Adequate described task materials, without a complete software/usability assessment. 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4, 7.2.5, 7.2.6, 7.2.7 = n/a: No paper-and-pencil or other non-digital administration is reviewed.\n8.1.1, 8.1.2, 8.1.3.1, 8.1.3.2, 8.1.3.3 = n/a: No reference-population norms or continuous norming are established. 8.1.4 = n/a: No AI norm-sampling procedure; the human puzzle study is not an AI norm sample. 8.2.1.1, 8.2.1.2, 8.2.1.3, 8.2.1.4, 8.2.1.5, 8.2.2 = n/a: No expert-set or empirically validated competence cutoff; exact-answer marking is not standard setting. 8.3.1, 8.3.2, 8.3.2.1, 8.3.2.2, 8.3.2.3, 8.3.3 = n/a for restricted raw-score comparison: EFPA permits this exception when norms are unnecessary for the use. This review restricts interpretation accordingly; it does not establish that broader claims satisfy that exception. Human difficulty matching, revision dates and public comparisons do not supply population norms or intelligence thresholds.\n9.1: No AI reliability coefficients or measurement-error estimates supplied. 9.2.1, 9.2.3 = 0; 9.2.2, 9.2.4 = no information: Internal consistency methods, values and sample suitability are unreported; its suitability for an overall reasoning interpretation is unresolved. 9.3.1, 9.3.2 = 0; 9.3.3, 9.3.4 = no information: No same-condition repeat study, intervals or matched AI samples. 9.4.1, 9.4.2 = 0; 9.4.3 = no information: Human-matched difficulty does not establish alternate-set precision for AI systems. 9.5.1, 9.5.2, 9.5.3 = n/a: No IRT scoring or precision model described. 9.6.1, 9.6.2, 9.6.3 = n/a: Exact-grid scoring involves no judgmental rating; software correctness is a separate concern. 9.7.1, 9.7.3 = 0; 9.7.2 = no method supplied: No alternative precision estimates. 9.8 = 0, critical: Precision for AI comparisons is unresolved. The 407 human participants, 515 sessions and item counts cannot substitute for AI reliability evidence.\n10.1 Content validity: Adequate support for assessing the selected grid-rule tasks, cross-referenced to 6.1; no separate numeric rating is prescribed here. 10.2.1 = no information; 10.2.2, 10.2.3 = 0: No dimensionality, invariance or DIF evidence for AI scores. 10.3.1.1: Human background-group analysis is described, but no corresponding AI validation design is established. 10.3.1.2 = 0: No explicit AI group hypotheses and supporting effects; the human null association does not establish AI equivalence. 10.3.1.3, 10.3.1.4 = 0: No convergent or discriminant correlations. 10.3.1.5 = n/a: No MTMM design. 10.3.1.6 = 0: No systematic instruction, representation or software manipulation study. 10.3.1.7 = n/a: No additional relationship method identified. 10.3.1.8, 10.3.1.9 = 0: AI validation sample adequacy and marker quality unreported. 10.3.1.10 = unknown: Validation study dates absent. 10.3.1.11 = 0: External relationship evidence insufficient.\n10.3.2.1 = not supplied; 10.3.2.2, 10.3.2.3, 10.3.2.4 = 0: No relevant external-outcome study, sample or criterion quality evidence. 10.3.2.5 = n/a: No qualitative diagnostic classification claim or validated cutoff is described. 10.3.2.6 = unknown: No criterion-study dates. 10.3.2.7 = 0: Broader reasoning implications lack criterion evidence in this packet. 10.4.1: Response-process relevance—design aims to discourage brute search and repeated-rule solutions. 10.4.2, 10.4.3 = 0: These intentions do not provide a systematic study showing how AI solutions were obtained. 10.5 = 0, critical for unfamiliar-rule reasoning and broader-intelligence interpretation: Content relevance exists, but the evidence does not establish that scores isolate the intended reasoning or generalise beyond grids. This does not invalidate reporting the observed exact-output score.\n11.1.1 = 2: Low-specialist-knowledge design supports broad task accessibility in intent. 11.1.2 = 2: Conditions and exposure restrictions support some fair-use guidance. 11.2 = 2: Content review and low-knowledge design address some access concerns; AI representation equivalence is untested. 11.3 = 0: Human background findings do not establish relevant AI subgroup piloting or DIF. 11.4, 11.5 = 0: Comparable AI precision and validity across system groups or representations are unestablished. 11.6.1, 11.6.2 = n/a: No norm or cutoff interpretation. 11.7 = 0: Report fairness cannot be assessed without report examples. 11.8 = 2: Adequate limited procedural support through verified settings and exposure rules; empirical fairness across AI groups remains unresolved.\n12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.6, 12.7 = 0: Taking digital result presentations as the report analogue, no three score-linked report examples are supplied to assess scope, consistency, interpretive validity, fairness, audience acceptability, detail or overall adequacy. This does not establish that an interpretive report product exists or is defective.\nFinal evaluation: Strengths are a clear grid task, explicit scoring, substantial human-informed development, public inspection materials and documented revisions. Limitations include scoring terminology ambiguity, missing AI precision, unestablished alternate-set equivalence, exposure uncertainty and absent evidence for broader generalisation. Under EFPA's critical-attribute rule, the 0 ratings for precision and claimed-use validity restrict use to research or exceptional expert interpretation; they indicate insufficient support, not demonstrated poor intrinsic quality. Users need competence in evaluation conditions, scoring and uncertainty; agreement with supplier qualification requirements cannot be assessed. Future work: Corrections are documented; further research or refinement plans are not supplied.\nSummary of section ratings: 6.4 = 2; 7.1.8 = 2; 7.2.7 = n/a; 8.3.3 = n/a for the restricted use; 9.8 = 0; 10.5 = 0; 11.8 = 2; 12.7 = 0. These are separate judgments, not an aggregate.\nPART C\nBibliography: European Federation of Psychologists' Associations AISBL (2025), Model for the Review, Description and Evaluation of Psychological and Educational Tests, version 5.0, https://www.efpa.eu/, CC BY-SA 4.0; supplied extraction only. Benchmark evidence: supplied ARC-AGI-2 passages, including their description of the technical report, scoring software, verified-testing rules and change record; complete bibliographic details absent. Referenced underlying works were not independently consulted.\nCoverage: All numbered descriptive fields and rated items are addressed, including nested technical subareas. No substantive omissions. The EFPA summary's 7.2.8 conflicts with the detailed form's 7.2.7; this review uses 7.2.7 and treats 7.2.8 as that summary cross-reference, not an additional rated item.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "Scores describe exact-output performance on the evaluated grid problems under the stated conditions.",
        "The official software permits fractional problem scores when only some new inputs are solved.",
        "Human piloting, duplicate-rule review and subsequent corrections support deliberate content development.",
        "Verified evaluations provide a more specified comparison context than unspecified community testing routes."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "The description's 'fully solved' criterion and software's fractional problem scoring can produce different interpretations of a score.",
        "The change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples, without recalculating every affected AI score.",
        "Public evaluation problems are exposed; hidden-test handling reduces but does not eliminate acknowledged exposure risk.",
        "Human difficulty matching does not demonstrate AI equivalence across the three test sets."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Repeated identical-condition evaluations, uncertainty estimates and sensitivity to instructions, representation and software.",
        "Final-item AI difficulty/discrimination data and evidence that high scores require the intended reasoning.",
        "External validation for language, social interaction, real-world work or comprehensive intelligence.",
        "Complete report examples, operational support details, AI subgroup validity and precision, and independently checked output archives."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "The test taker is an AI system under specified settings; human participant data inform development rather than serving as AI norms.",
        "Human administration categories become evaluation-control descriptions; grid processing replaces human sensory and motor prerequisites.",
        "Human disability, professional credentials and debriefing questions are inapplicable as AI attributes; operator requirements and stakeholder communication remain relevant.",
        "Fair use concerns comparable conditions, representation and exposure across AI systems; it is not a claim that AI systems have human demographic characteristics.",
        "Norms are inapplicable only to the restricted raw-performance comparison adopted here; competence thresholds and broader intelligence interpretations remain unsupported.",
        "Digital result presentations are provisionally treated as report analogues. Their absence from the packet yields 0, not a finding of defective reports.",
        "EFPA's human sample-size and coefficient examples are not mechanically applied to puzzle counts or human pilot sessions."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Clarify 'fully solved' versus the software's averaged input credit, and specify the exact instructions, grid representation, version and evaluation conditions. The record documents earlier unclear examples but does not establish how many unclear questions remain."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "Application: Original EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, applied to the supplied DesignQA passages. Ratings: n/a = inapplicable; 0 = insufficient information; 1 = inadequate; 2 = adequate; 3 = good; 4 = excellent. Ratings concern the supplied evidence, not uninspected materials. Section judgments are not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated.\nPART A\n1. Factual description: Reviewer = simulated AI benchmark-reviewer perspective; current review date = not supplied; source inspection date = 6 October 2026; previous review date = not supplied. Instrument name and short name = DesignQA. Scope = original benchmark described in the 2024 paper and public scoring software. Original name for a local adaptation, local adaptation authors and adaptation publication date = n/a. Authors = researchers and engineers; individual names absent. Local distributor/publisher and separate original publisher = not identified. Original paper year = 2024; exact benchmark release date and current software revision date = not supplied.\n2.1 Content domains: Other—engineering-rule retrieval, drawing understanding, rule application. 2.2 Area of use: Other—AI engineering-document evaluation. 2.3 Intended population: AI systems answering engineering-document questions; formal eligibility boundaries absent. 2.4 Intended users: Researchers and AI evaluators inferred from intended use; formal publisher-defined classes absent. 2.5 Scales: Six task groups—individual-rule retrieval, related-rule gathering, technical-term explanation, component presence, dimensional compliance and performance compliance—plus an equal-group-weight overall score. Distinct underlying skills are unestablished. 2.6 Response mode: Digitally generated text or yes/no answers, sometimes with explanations. 2.7 Demands: Human attention, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities and digital experience are n/a as human attributes. Language command, language fluency, reading and writing are reinterpreted as processing rules/questions and producing text; required proficiency limits are absent. Human vision is n/a; image/drawing processing is relevant and explicitly required for some tasks, but capability limits are unspecified. Other—technical terminology and dimension interpretation are required by described tasks. 2.8 Conditions: Systems may receive a whole rulebook or retrieved passages; instructions and settings are described in the paper, but historical configurations are not fully linked to results. 2.9 Response types: Open text and yes/no selection, with some generated explanations. 2.10 Stimuli: Text, vehicle images and drawings. 2.11 Items: 1,451 question-answer pairs across six groups; individual-rule retrieval has 1,192 and performance compliance 16. Counts for the other four groups are not supplied; one released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding paper count. 2.12.1 Administration: Individual AI-system evaluation, reinterpreting individual administration; group administration unestablished. 2.12.2 Mode of use: Research-controlled evaluations are described, but no formal supervision, identity-control or certification regime is established. 2.13 Technology: Digital model execution and scoring; retrieval software for some conditions. Exact hardware/connectivity requirements absent. 2.14 Time: Preparation, administration, analysis and feedback times unreported. Scoring is automated, so manual scoring time is 0 under EFPA's convention, not zero computational runtime. 2.15 Forms: Different information-supply and image/dimension manipulations are conditions, not demonstrated parallel forms. Later changes may affect results; subset equivalence and independent interpretability are unestablished. 2.16 Determination: Fixed question collection; no response-adaptive item selection described. 2.17 Informant: Other—the evaluated AI's answers, not human self-report.\n3.1 Scoring procedure: Digital comparison with supplied answers. 3.2 Scores: Text similarity for some answers/explanations and correctness for yes/no decisions; overall score equally weights six groups despite unequal sizes and different metrics. Exact formulas are not reproduced. 3.3 Scales: Task-specific raw metrics and an equal-weight composite; no standard scores or competence cutoffs established. 3.4 Standard-score transformation: n/a. 3.5 Norming: No differentiated norms described; random and AI baselines are comparison results, not population norms.\n4.1 Digitally generated reports: Software generates scores and some responses are public; a distinct interpretive report system and number of report types are unestablished. 4.2 Description: Overall and task-group results, with some AI responses. 4.3 Presentation: Full report format absent. 4.4 Structure: Task-group and overall scoring; narrative structure unknown. 4.5 Context sensitivity: Unknown. 4.6 Development: Metric aggregation described, but report-content development unknown. 4.7 Modifiability: Unknown. 4.8 Transparency: Equal-group aggregation is described; mappings to competence interpretations are unvalidated. 4.9 Content: Task-performance results; general engineering competence predictions are unestablished. 4.10 Recipients: Researchers/evaluators inferred; formal recipient categories absent.\n5.1 Supporting information: Paper, public questions, instructions, scoring code, small marking-test files and some model responses. 5.2 Publication: Public digital materials; precise formats not fully specified. 5.3 Qualifications: Supplier requirements unclear; no qualification requirement can be inferred. A licence file and complete reuse rules were not found in the inspected materials, which does not establish that permission is unavailable.\nGeneral description: DesignQA evaluates AI answers to questions grounded in Formula SAE rules, vehicle materials and test data. Six unevenly sized groups cover retrieval, explanation, component recognition and compliance assessment. Text-similarity and decision-correctness metrics support group results, and public software equally weights the groups in an overall score. Information supplied to models varies across some comparisons. The benchmark addresses selected tasks from one rulebook; norms, validated latent skill scales and transfer to other engineering documents are not established in the supplied evidence.\nPART B\nInformation sources: Only the supplied benchmark passages and EFPA extraction; no underlying paper, files, software or results independently inspected for this review. No confidential publisher evidence was used.\n6.1.1 = 2: Six practical task types operationalise the intended document-understanding activities, without establishing a unified competence construct. 6.1.2 = 2: Model comparisons and input manipulations provide task-related empirical context, but broader construct research is limited. 6.1.3.1 = 1: The overall design mixes unequal task samples and unlike marking methods without demonstrated interpretation, and some comparisons change information supply. 6.1.3.2 = 2: Real materials and practitioner/researcher contributions support content relevance; coverage is restricted. 6.1.3.3 = 2: Additional review of manually written questions is described, but exceptions and limited explanation checks constrain final-pool assurance. 6.1.4 = n/a: No translated/local adaptation reviewed. 6.1.5: Psychometric framework unspecified; group results and sensitivity analyses are described, but item discrimination, calibrated difficulty, distractor and DIF indices are absent. 6.1.6, 6.1.7 = 0: Systematic psychometric item-analysis methods and results are insufficiently supplied. 6.1.8 = 2: Practical task development is adequately motivated, while composite design and scoring need further justification.\n6.2.1 = 3: Task rationale and stated scope limits are clear. 6.2.2 = 2: Sources and review procedures are described, with incomplete final-item checks. 6.2.3 = n/a: No translation/adaptation. 6.2.4 = 1: Exact historical inputs, settings and software are not fully linked to each result, limiting repeatability. 6.2.5 = n/a: No normative interpretation established for restricted raw-score comparisons. 6.2.6 = 0: Identical-condition precision documentation insufficient. 6.2.7 = 2: Practical content rationale and reviewer checks are described, but agreement and residual-error evidence are absent. 6.2.8, 6.2.9 = 0: Internal-structure and external-relationship validation documentation insufficient. 6.2.10 = 2: Input manipulations and scoring examples document some alternative influences. 6.2.11 = 2: Different information conditions and limitations are acknowledged, but comprehensive comparison guidance is absent. 6.2.12 = 0: Interpretive report documentation absent. 6.2.13 = 0: Full user-documentation language cannot be assessed from the summary. 6.2.14 = 2: Basic tasks and scoring are documented, with material reproducibility gaps.\n6.3.1 = 2: Instructions and settings are described, but complete historical reconstruction is unavailable. 6.3.2 = 2: Marking methods and some checks are documented, including limitations; correct implementation across all cases is unestablished. 6.3.3 = n/a: No norm conversion. 6.3.4 = 2: The paper acknowledges narrow scope and imperfect marking; detailed uncertainty-based interpretation is missing. 6.3.5 = 0: Stakeholder feedback guidance absent; human test-taker debriefing is n/a. 6.3.6 = 0: Operational guidance for fair comparison across exposure, retrieval and modality conditions is insufficient. 6.3.7 = 0: Rules for training on questions, repeat submissions and responsible reuse are insufficiently available. 6.3.8 = 0: Complete technical requirements, error recovery and support not supplied. 6.3.9 = 2: The original paper and public material types are identified, but complete references and result-to-artifact links are absent. 6.3.10 = 2: Basic procedures are described; reproducibility and reuse guidance require improvement. 6.4 = 2: Adequate basic rationale/documentation with documented operational limitations.\n7.1.1 = 0: Small marking tests do not establish whole-system robustness. 7.1.2, 7.1.3 = 2: The six task types, response requirements and availability of instructions support basic intelligibility. 7.1.4 = 1: Documented wording and formatting effects can penalise substantively relevant responses. 7.1.5 = 0: Interface design not supplied. 7.1.6 = n/a: Human disability accessibility is not an AI test-taker attribute; modality compatibility remains relevant separately. 7.1.7 = 2: Authentic rules and drawings support practical content quality, but answer completeness and review coverage are limited. 7.1.8 = 2: Materials support exploratory task evaluation, with specific scoring/answer defects. 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4, 7.2.5, 7.2.6, 7.2.7 = n/a: No paper-and-pencil or non-digital administration is reviewed.\n8.1.1, 8.1.2, 8.1.3.1, 8.1.3.2, 8.1.3.3 = n/a: No reference-population norms or continuous norming. 8.1.4 = n/a: No norm-sampling procedure; the question collection is not a norm sample. 8.2.1.1, 8.2.1.2, 8.2.1.3, 8.2.1.4, 8.2.1.5, 8.2.2 = n/a: No AI competence threshold is set by expert judgments or external-outcome studies. Checking whether a depicted design complies with a rule is an item task, not standard setting for AI competence. 8.3.1, 8.3.2, 8.3.2.1, 8.3.2.2, 8.3.2.3, 8.3.3 = n/a for restricted task-score comparison: EFPA permits a raw-score-use exception when population norms and cutoffs are unnecessary. This does not authorise broader competence interpretation or establish that the original documentation expressly limits use to ranking.\n9.1: No reliability coefficients or measurement-error estimates for main comparisons supplied; changed-passage variation is described separately. 9.2.1, 9.2.2, 9.2.3, 9.2.4 = n/a for the heterogeneous six-group composite: EFPA excludes internal consistency for heterogeneous scales. For any within-group homogeneous-skill interpretation, suitability and evidence are unresolved rather than established. 9.3.1, 9.3.2 = 0; 9.3.3, 9.3.4 = no information: No identical-condition retest study, intervals or matched retest samples. 9.4.1, 9.4.2 = 0; 9.4.3 = no information: Changed passages and images are not validated equivalent forms. 9.5.1, 9.5.2, 9.5.3 = n/a: No IRT model described. 9.6.1, 9.6.2, 9.6.3 = n/a for automated response scoring: Human answer-authoring/review judgments are relevant to content and answer-key validity, but reviewer agreement is unreported; no human response-rating procedure is established. 9.7.1 = 0; 9.7.2: One AI tested using five passage sets, with other input manipulations also described; 9.7.3 = 0: This supplies sensitivity information, but no adequate precision estimate for identical-condition main comparisons. 9.8 = 0, critical: Main-score precision is insufficiently established. The 1,451 questions are not 1,451 independent tested systems, and the 16-item group has coarse accuracy resolution.\n10.1 Content validity: Real engineering materials and task-oriented design support relevance within the selected Formula SAE activities; one rulebook, uneven groups and incomplete review constrain representativeness.
